new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

message.description: Your full report for your caller

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Exit code 1
     1	# Trade Blotter
     2	
     3	A single-page trade blotter: enter trades, see them in a sortable grid, see positions derived from trade history.
     4	
     5	The approved design is authoritative: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-trade-blotter-design.md`. Read it before changing behavior. `prompt.md` is the original prompt; where it differs, the design wins (no users, no client timestamps, no timezone setting, no paste mode).
     6	
     7	## Requirements summary
     8	
     9	- Backend: .NET 8 REST API, SQLite via EF Core. `POST /trades` (201 + Location), `GET /trades` (newest first), `GET /trades/{id}`, `GET /positions` (net quantity and average cost per symbol, sorted by symbol, zero positions omitted). Positions are computed, never stored.
    10	- Frontend: Vue 3 `<script setup>` + TS, Vite, Pinia, PrimeVue, AG Grid Community. Toolbar (search + "+"), blotter grid, positions panel, trade entry modal.
    11	- Errors are RFC 7807 ProblemDetails. JSON is camelCase. Timestamps are UTC with a `Z` suffix.
    12	
    13	## Architecture rules
    14	
    15	- Backend: Controller → Feature. Controllers only translate HTTP; business logic and data access live in `Features/<Name>/`.
    16	- `decimal` for quantity and price on the server, end to end. Never `double` or `float` for money.
    17	- Frontend: shared state lives in Pinia stores (`src/stores`). Components read stores; `src/api` holds stateless fetch calls.
    18	- Layout uses CSS `display: grid`.
    19	- AG Grid Community only; no Enterprise features.
    20	
    21	## Quality rules
    22	
    23	- Unit test coverage must stay at or above 80% lines (enforced by coverlet and Vitest thresholds).
    24	- Files have a soft 500-line limit. `scripts/check-file-length.sh` warns; split the file rather than ignore it.
    25	- Use TDD for logic.
    26	- Mutation testing runs on demand (`npm run mutation`, `dotnet stryker`), never on a hook.
    27	- Update `README.md` whenever configuration changes (tooling, scripts, ports, env vars, dependencies).
    28	
    29	## Commit rules
    30	
    31	- One meaningful change per commit.
    32	- Short imperative subject line (e.g. "Add position calculator").
    33	- Pre-commit runs formatters, linters, the file-length check, and tests for the side that changed. Don't bypass it with `--no-verify`.
    34	
    35	## Section ownership
    36	
    37	Parallel agents edit only their own sections of this file and `README.md`:
    38	
    39	- Backend agent: `backend/` and the sections marked **Backend**.
    40	- Frontend agent: `frontend/` and the sections marked **Frontend**.
    41	- Coordinator: everything else (root config, `docs/`, e2e, shared sections).
    42	
    43	## Backend
    44	
    45	<!-- Owned by the backend agent. -->
    46	
    47	- Trade validation goes in `Features/Trades/TradeValidator` (runs via `IValidatableObject`), not in controllers or attributes that change `docs/openapi.json`.
    48	- Inject `TimeProvider`; tests use `FakeTimeProvider`. Never call `DateTime.UtcNow` in features.
    49	- `PositionCalculator` stays pure and unrounded; rounding to 6 places happens in `PositionService`.
    50	- Integration tests that write data get their own `ApiFactory`; `ContractTests` assumes an empty DB.
    51	
    52	## Frontend
    53	
    54	<!-- Owned by the frontend agent. -->
    55	
    56	- Pure logic lives in `src/lib/` and column defs in `src/components/*Columns.ts`, so they test without mounting a grid. Components stay thin.
    57	- Grid custom components are registered by name with `defineExpose` (see `BlotterGrid.vue`).
    58	- AG Grid rows animate out after a filter or data change. Component tests wait about 600 ms before asserting that a row is gone.
    59	- `npm run dev:mock` runs the UI without the backend (`mock/mockApi.ts`, dev-only). Keep it in step with `docs/openapi.json`.
    60	- Biome runs with `html.experimentalFullSupportEnabled` so it sees template usage in `.vue` files.

Exit code 1
     1	Check trade-blotter-exercise in downloads folder. We are going to develop this application in parallel using herdr to create multiple sessions + worktrees. 
     2	
     3	First, create a GitHub repository that is public. Add this prompt (saved as prompt.md in downloads) into the repository. 
     4	
     5	We will do this in 3 parts. 
     6	1. Creating the skeleton project with C# and Vue frontend (1 agent)
     7	2. Creating .NET backend (1 agent) as well as Vue frontend (1 agent) in full.
     8	3. Merging both pieces, then doing a full e2e test using playwright. 
     9	
    10	Part 1. Skeleton project
    11	This is the part where we add data models, set up libraries, as well as mutation testing frameworks, and CLAUDE.md + hooks. Each top bullet item is practically a commit. 
    12	
    13	- Create CLAUDE.md file based on the requirements file. Add prompt-based rules as well as commit guidelines. Commits should cover one meaningful feature at a time and should be concise and to the point in the message. Create a README.md skeleton that CLAUDE.md specifies will need to be filled out every time configuration changes. We will specify at least 80% test coverage for unit tests.
    14	- Install relevant skills and MCP servers for the project. AG-grid is one. 
    15	- We will use Stryker.NET and maybe Stryker.js for mutation testing. I suspect they will be more useful for the backend, and we probably don't need it for frontend.
    16	- Hooks must lint every file that is touched. For linting, we will use Biome for js and CSharpier for C#. Commits should run tests and linters. 
    17	- We need other developer friendly tools, custom or otherwise, that prevents files from being over 500 lines long as a soft limit. Use knip, jscpd, etc. 
    18	- Create skeleton endpoints for POST, GET. 
    19	  - Submitting a new trade requires, symbol, side, quantity, price, timestamp. Optionally requires timezone.
    20	  - Getting trades requires no parameters.
    21	  - Getting positions requires no parameters.
    22	  - In an ideal world we would be adding server side pagination. But it introduces a lot of questions about missing data in-between fetches, especially if we add sorting & filtering. So we will just return everything for now. 
    23	- Create data models and set up the local database. 
    24	  - A trade record:
    25	    {
    26	    	uid: uuid
    27	    	userId: uuid, foreign key
    28	    	symbol: string
    29	    	side: Enum {Buy, Sell} // question- will other types exist at all?
    30	    	quantity: double
    31	    	price: double
    32	    	timestamp: DateTime // stored in UTC, api should accept timezone info (assume NYC if empty) and convert.
    33	    } 
    34	  - Positions (assumed always current). Does a dictionary over symbols as keys work better here?
    35	    {
    36	    	symbol: string
    37	    	net_quantity: double
    38	    	avg_price: double 
    39	    }
    40	    We can just use weighted averages to compute positions. Since net position is a double value, we will need to define 0 as anything less than a cent.
    41	  - User:
    42	    {
    43	    	uid: uuid
    44	    	id: string // not adding password - not really in scope. This is just for storing settings
    45	    	timezone: string, default nyc (derived from TimeZoneInfo)
    46	    }
    47	- Use SQLite for this. We will use EF to query for these datasets. The table should easily fall out based on the above data models. 
    48	
    49	Part 2. Create backend & frontend
    50	This part can be parallelized fairly easily. 
    51

1	# Trade Blotter — Design
     2	
     3	## Intent
     4	
     5	A take-home exercise: a trade blotter where a user enters trades, sees them in a live table, and sees positions derived from trade history. Graded on domain modeling, API design, Vue patterns, UI judgment, tests, and repo quality. "Quality over completeness." The exercise also requires building with Claude Code and committing the full transcript.
     6	
     7	The build is also a demonstration of parallel agent work: a coordinator (this session) drives three herdr agent sessions: one for Part 1 on `main`, then two for Part 2 in worktrees.
     8	
     9	## Requirements (restated from the exercise)
    10	
    11	- Backend: C# / .NET 8 REST API. `POST /trades`, `GET /trades` (newest first), `GET /positions` (net qty, avg cost per symbol). Positions derived, never stored. Zero net position omitted. SQLite.
    12	- Frontend: Vue 3 Composition API, Pinia for state, Vite. Trade entry form (symbol, side, quantity, price; no empty fields; quantity and price positive). Blotter updates without page reload. Columns: timestamp, symbol, side, quantity, price, notional. Sortable. Side visually distinct. Positions panel updates reactively on submit.
    13	- Tests: at least position calculation. README with setup, assumptions, and what's next. Clear commit history. Public GitHub repo. Full transcript included.
    14	
    15	## Goals
    16	
    17	- Correct average-cost position logic, proven by unit tests and mutation testing.
    18	- A clean, small API contract with proper status codes and ProblemDetails errors.
    19	- A scannable, pleasant single-page blotter.
    20	- Guardrails that keep agent output tidy: lint on every edit, tests and lint on every commit, 80% unit coverage, soft 500-line file limit, duplication and dead-code checks.
    21	
    22	## Non-goals
    23	
    24	- Authentication, users, per-user settings.
    25	- Server-side pagination, sorting, or filtering. All trades are returned; the grid sorts and filters client-side. (Pagination raises consistency questions between fetches once sorting and filtering exist.)
    26	- Bulk/paste trade entry.
    27	- Real-time push (SSE/WebSockets). "Live" means the grid refreshes after the user's own submissions.
    28	- Market data, P&L, realized gains.
    29	- Client-supplied timestamps or timezone handling on the server.
    30	
    31	## Anti-goals
    32	
    33	- Floating-point money. Quantity and price are `decimal` end to end on the server.
    34	- Business logic in controllers, or state scattered across components instead of Pinia.
    35	- Enterprise-only AG Grid features.
    36	
    37	## Decisions
    38	
    39	### Domain
    40	
    41	**Trade**
    42	
    43	| Field | Type | Notes |
    44	|---|---|---|
    45	| `Id` | `Guid` | Server-generated |
    46	| `Sequence` | `long` | Autoincrement; internal tiebreak for equal timestamps (Guids don't preserve insertion order). Not in the API. |
    47	| `Symbol` | `string` | Trimmed, upper-cased. 1–10 chars, `^[A-Z0-9.\-]+$` |
    48	| `Side` | `enum Side { Buy, Sell }` | Serialized as `"Buy"` / `"Sell"`. A short is just a negative net position; no short-sell or cover types. |
    49	| `Quantity` | `decimal` | > 0, ≤ 1,000,000,000, at most 4 decimal places (fractional shares allowed) |
    50	| `Price` | `decimal` | > 0, ≤ 1,000,000,000, at most 4 decimal places |
    51	| `Timestamp` | `DateTime` (UTC) | Set by the server at insert (`DateTime.UtcNow` via an injected `TimeProvider` for testability). Never accepted from the client. |
    52	
    53	No `User` entity, no `UserId`.
    54	
    55	**Position** (computed, not persisted)
    56	
    57	| Field | Type |
    58	|---|---|
    59	| `Symbol` | `string` |
    60	| `NetQuantity` | `decimal` (negative = short) |
    61	| `AverageCost` | `decimal` |
    62	
    63	Computed internally with a dictionary keyed by symbol; returned as an array sorted by symbol. Positions whose net quantity is exactly `0` are omitted (exact because of `decimal`; no epsilon).
    64	
    65	**Average-cost rule.** Process each symbol's trades in timestamp order (ties broken by `Sequence`). Let signed quantity be `+q` for Buy, `-q` for Sell.
    66	
    67	- Trade increases the absolute position (same direction, or from flat): `avg = (|net| * avg + q * price) / (|net| + q)`.
    68	- Trade reduces the position without crossing zero: `avg` unchanged.
    69	- Trade closes exactly to zero: position removed; next trade starts fresh.
    70	- Trade crosses zero (flip): `avg = price` of that trade; new net is the remainder.
    71	
    72	Worked examples that must be unit tests:
    73	
    74	| Trades | Net | Avg |
    75	|---|---|---|
    76	| Buy 100 @ 10, Buy 100 @ 20 | 200 | 15 |
    77	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 40 @ 50 | 60 | 10 |
    78	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 100 @ 12 | omitted | — |
    79	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 150 @ 12 | -50 | 12 |
    80	| Sell 50 @ 20, Sell 50 @ 10 | -100 | 15 |
    81	| Sell 100 @ 20, Buy 30 @ 5 | -70 | 20 |
    82	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 100 @ 12, Buy 10 @ 30 | 10 | 30 |
    83	
    84	The calculator works unrounded; the API rounds `AverageCost` to 6 decimal places (midpoint away from zero) so values survive JavaScript's `number` parsing. Money is sent as JSON numbers, not strings. The frontend formats for display. (My call.)
    85	
    86	### API contract
    87	
    88	All JSON, camelCase. Errors use RFC 7807 ProblemDetails.
    89	
    90	`POST /trades`
    91	
    92	```json
    93	{ "symbol": "AAPL", "side": "Buy", "quantity": 100, "price": 187.25 }
    94	```
    95	
    96	- `201 Created`, `Location: /trades/{id}`, body = the created trade.
    97	- `400` ValidationProblemDetails for missing/invalid fields, unknown side, malformed JSON.
    98	- `415` for non-JSON content type (framework default).
    99	
   100	`GET /trades` → `200`, array of trades, newest first (`Timestamp` desc, then `Sequence` desc):
   101	
   102	```json
   103	[{ "id": "…", "symbol": "AAPL", "side": "Buy", "quantity": 100, "price": 187.25, "timestamp": "2026-10-19T14:03:11.123Z" }]
   104	```
   105	
   106	`GET /positions` → `200`, array sorted by symbol:
   107	
   108	```json
   109	[{ "symbol": "AAPL", "netQuantity": 100, "averageCost": 187.25 }]
   110	```
   111	
   112	Unhandled exceptions → `500` ProblemDetails, no stack trace outside Development. `GET /trades/{id}` is not required; `Location` still points there (my call: implement it as a trivial endpoint so the header is honest).
   113	
   114	Timestamps always serialize with a `Z` suffix. SQLite loses `DateTimeKind`, so the EF model needs a value converter that marks reads as UTC.
   115	
   116	Notional (`quantity * price`) is computed in the frontend, not sent by the API.
   117	
   118	Part 1 commits this contract as DTOs plus an OpenAPI document (Swashbuckle, exported to `docs/openapi.json`) and example payloads, so the frontend agent can build against a mock without waiting on the backend.
   119	
   120	### Backend architecture
   121	
   122	UI → Controller → Feature (business logic + data access).
   123	
   124	```
   125	backend/
   126	  TradeBlotter.sln
   127	  src/TradeBlotter.Api/
   128	    Controllers/        TradesController, PositionsController — HTTP only
   129	    Features/Trades/    trade service, request/response DTOs, validation
   130	    Features/Positions/ PositionCalculator (pure function), positions service
   131	    Data/               AppDbContext, entity config, migrations
   132	    Program.cs
   133	  tests/TradeBlotter.Api.Tests/   xUnit; unit + WebApplicationFactory integration tests
   134	```
   135	
   136	- EF Core 8 with SQLite, migrations committed. DB file `backend/src/TradeBlotter.Api/trade-blotter.db`, gitignored; connection string overridable via config/env (e2e uses a throwaway file).
   137	- SQLite stores `decimal` as TEXT and can't order or sum it in SQL. That's fine: positions are computed in memory. Order trades by `Timestamp` (ISO text sorts correctly).
   138	- `PositionCalculator` is a pure static function over a list of trades; it is the main mutation-testing target.
   139	
   140	### Frontend architecture
   141	
   142	```
   143	frontend/
   144	  src/
   145	    api/            fetch wrapper + trades/positions calls (no state)
   146	    stores/         Pinia: trades, positions
   147	    components/     Toolbar, BlotterGrid, SideCellRenderer, PositionsPanel, TradeEntryModal, TradeForm
   148	    App.vue, main.ts
   149	  e2e/              Playwright (Part 3)
   150	```
   151	
   152	- Vue 3 `<script setup>` + TypeScript, Vite, Pinia, PrimeVue (one theme preset, soft palette), AG Grid Community (`ag-grid-vue3`).
   153	- Layout uses CSS `display: grid` throughout: toolbar row on top, blotter in the main area, positions panel beside it.
   154	- Toolbar: search box (drives an AG Grid external filter via `isExternalFilterPresent` / `doesExternalFilterPass`) and a "+" button that opens the trade entry modal.
   155	- Blotter columns default to newest first, all sortable. Side uses a custom cell renderer: green Buy, red Sell. Timestamps are converted from UTC to the browser's local timezone with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.
   156	- Trade entry modal (PrimeVue Dialog) holds a single form: symbol, side, quantity, price. Small labels above inputs. Client-side validation mirrors the server's. Paste/bulk entry was considered and dropped (AG Grid's multi-cell paste is Enterprise-only).
   157	- Search box matches symbol and side, case-insensitive substring. (My call.)
   158	- After any successful POST  the trades and positions stores both re-fetch everything from the server. No optimistic insert, no `since` parameter.
   159	- Errors surface via PrimeVue Toast.
   160	- Dev server proxies `/trades` and `/positions` to the backend (no CORS config needed).
   161	- No timezone setting, no seed data.
   162	
   163	### Tooling and guardrails
   164	
   165	| Concern | Tool |
   166	|---|---|
   167	| C# format/lint | CSharpier |
   168	| JS/TS/Vue format/lint | Biome |
   169	| Unit tests | xUnit (backend), Vitest (frontend) |
   170	| Coverage ≥ 80% lines, enforced | coverlet threshold (backend), Vitest coverage thresholds (frontend) |
   171	| Mutation testing | Stryker.NET (backend `Features/**`), Stryker.js (frontend `src/stores`, `src/api`, pure helpers) |
   172	| Dead code / unused deps | knip |
   173	| Duplication | jscpd (both trees) |
   174	| File length | custom script: warn above 500 lines (soft; never blocks) |
   175	| Git hooks | lefthook |
   176	
   177	**Claude Code hooks** (`.claude/settings.json`): PostToolUse on Edit/Write/MultiEdit runs a script that formats and lints the touched file (Biome for `.ts/.js/.vue/.json`, CSharpier for `.cs`), then runs the file-length check. Lint errors exit 2 so the agent sees them.
   178	
   179	**Pre-commit** (lefthook): Biome and CSharpier on staged files, file-length check, then tests only for the side that changed (backend tests if `backend/**` is staged, frontend tests if `frontend/**`). knip and jscpd run on pre-push, not pre-commit, to keep commits fast.
   180	
   181	**Mutation testing is never on a hook.** Run on demand via scripts. Configure for speed:
   182	
   183	- Stryker.js: `stryker.config.mjs` with `testRunner: "vitest"`, `concurrency: os.availableParallelism() - 1`, `incremental: true` (incremental file gitignored), `ignoreStatic: true`, `mutate` restricted to logic files (exclude `.vue`, components, `main.ts`), no TypeScript checker. The vitest runner uses per-test coverage automatically.
   184	- Stryker.NET: `stryker-config.json` with `concurrency` set to cores − 1, `mutate` restricted to `Features/**`, `coverage-analysis: perTest`, `since` mode available for incremental runs. Installed as a local dotnet tool (`.config/dotnet-tools.json`).
   185	- Thresholds: high 80, low 60, break 50 for both.
   186	
   187	**MCP servers and skills** (`.mcp.json`, project-scoped): AG Grid, PrimeVue, Playwright. Verify package names at install time; drop any that don't exist rather than substituting a lookalike.
   188	
   189	### Repo files
   190	
   191	- `CLAUDE.md`: requirements summary, architecture rules (Controller → Feature, Pinia for state, `decimal` money, grid layout), commit rules (one meaningful change per commit, short imperative message), coverage rule, "update README whenever configuration changes", per-part section ownership.
   192	- `README.md`: setup (backend, frontend, tests, mutation, e2e), assumptions and design decisions, what's next. Skeleton in Part 1; each agent adds to its own section only.
   193	- `prompt.md`: the coordinator prompt, committed as-is.
   194	- `transcripts/`: every session's Claude Code `.jsonl` transcript, copied at the end, named by part. Scanned for secrets and absolute home paths before commit.
   195	- `.gitignore`: `bin/`, `obj/`, `node_modules/`, `*.db`, Stryker output and incremental files, Playwright reports.
   196	
   197	## Execution plan (coordination)
   198	
   199	Repo: `ensj/trade-blotter`, public. `main` is the integration branch.
   200	
   201	**Part 1 — skeleton (1 agent, on `main`).** Roughly one commit per bullet in `prompt.md`'s Part 1. A scaffold commit (empty .NET solution + test project, Vite app) goes right after CLAUDE.md so later configs have something to point at. Order: CLAUDE.md + README skeleton; project scaffold; skills/MCP; mutation testing config; hooks + linters; dev tools (knip, jscpd, file length); skeleton endpoints + DTOs + OpenAPI; data model + SQLite + EF migration. Skeleton endpoints return `501` or empty arrays. Coverage gates apply from the first commit with tests. Exit criteria: both projects build, hooks fire, pre-commit passes, OpenAPI committed.
   202	
   203	**Part 2 — parallel (2 agents, 2 worktrees).** Branches `feat/backend` and `feat/frontend` off Part 1's `main`. Each agent touches only its own tree plus its own README/CLAUDE.md section.
   204	
   205	- Backend: implement endpoints via features; position calculator with the worked-example tests; mutation testing on features; error handling and status codes.
   206	- Frontend: grid layout; AG Grid blotter with side renderer and external filter; Pinia stores + API module; toolbar and trade entry modal; positions panel; PrimeVue theme. Builds against a mock of the committed contract.
   207	
   208	**Part 3 — integrate and verify (coordinator + subagents, no extra herdr session).** Merge both branches into `main`. Playwright e2e against the real backend on a fresh DB, with screenshots of the full flow. A UI review pass on the screenshots (spacing, column order for a trader, label placement, grid sizing, consistent soft theme). A structure review (folders, Controller → Feature boundaries). Coverage subagents check every requirement in the exercise and `prompt.md` against the result. Copy transcripts, finish README, push.
   209	
   210	## Prerequisite
   211	
   212	.NET 8 SDK is not installed (only 6.0.401). Install it before Part 1.
   213	
   214	## Left to the builder
   215	
   216	- Exact AG Grid / PrimeVue theme values, within "soft hue, consistent".
   217	- Column widths and default column order (Part 3 reviews it).
   218	- Test file organization within each test project.
   219	- Exact jscpd threshold and knip config.

    27	- Real-time push (SSE/WebSockets). "Live" means the grid refreshes after the user's own submissions.
    28	- Market data, P&L, realized gains.
    29	- Client-supplied timestamps or timezone handling on the server.
    30	
    31	## Anti-goals
    32	
    33	- Floating-point money. Quantity and price are `decimal` end to end on the server.
    34	- Business logic in controllers, or state scattered across components instead of Pinia.
    35	- Enterprise-only AG Grid features.
    36	
    37	## Decisions
    38	
    39	### Domain
    40	
    41	**Trade**
    42	
    43	| Field | Type | Notes |
    44	|---|---|---|
    45	| `Id` | `Guid` | Server-generated |
    46	| `Sequence` | `long` | Autoincrement; internal tiebreak for equal timestamps (Guids don't preserve insertion order). Not in the API. |
    47	| `Symbol` | `string` | Trimmed, upper-cased. 1–10 chars, `^[A-Z0-9.\-]+$` |
    48	| `Side` | `enum Side { Buy, Sell }` | Serialized as `"Buy"` / `"Sell"`. A short is just a negative net position; no short-sell or cover types. |
    49	| `Quantity` | `decimal` | > 0, ≤ 1,000,000,000, at most 4 decimal places (fractional shares allowed) |
    50	| `Price` | `decimal` | > 0, ≤ 1,000,000,000, at most 4 decimal places |
    51	| `Timestamp` | `DateTime` (UTC) | Set by the server at insert (`DateTime.UtcNow` via an injected `TimeProvider` for testability). Never accepted from the client. |
    52	
    53	No `User` entity, no `UserId`.
    54	
    55	**Position** (computed, not persisted)
    56	
    57	| Field | Type |
    58	|---|---|
    59	| `Symbol` | `string` |
    60	| `NetQuantity` | `decimal` (negative = short) |
    61	| `AverageCost` | `decimal` |
    62	
    63	Computed internally with a dictionary keyed by symbol; returned as an array sorted by symbol. Positions whose net quantity is exactly `0` are omitted (exact because of `decimal`; no epsilon).
    64	
    65	**Average-cost rule.** Process each symbol's trades in timestamp order (ties broken by `Sequence`). Let signed quantity be `+q` for Buy, `-q` for Sell.
    66	
    67	- Trade increases the absolute position (same direction, or from flat): `avg = (|net| * avg + q * price) / (|net| + q)`.
    68	- Trade reduces the position without crossing zero: `avg` unchanged.
    69	- Trade closes exactly to zero: position removed; next trade starts fresh.
    70	- Trade crosses zero (flip): `avg = price` of that trade; new net is the remainder.
    71	
    72	Worked examples that must be unit tests:
    73	
    74	| Trades | Net | Avg |
    75	|---|---|---|
    76	| Buy 100 @ 10, Buy 100 @ 20 | 200 | 15 |
    77	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 40 @ 50 | 60 | 10 |
    78	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 100 @ 12 | omitted | — |
    79	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 150 @ 12 | -50 | 12 |
    80	| Sell 50 @ 20, Sell 50 @ 10 | -100 | 15 |
    81	| Sell 100 @ 20, Buy 30 @ 5 | -70 | 20 |
    82	| Buy 100 @ 10, Sell 100 @ 12, Buy 10 @ 30 | 10 | 30 |
    83	
    84	The calculator works unrounded; the API rounds `AverageCost` to 6 decimal places (midpoint away from zero) so values survive JavaScript's `number` parsing. Money is sent as JSON numbers, not strings. The frontend formats for display. (My call.)
    85	
    86	### API contract
    87	
    88	All JSON, camelCase. Errors use RFC 7807 ProblemDetails.
    89	
    90	`POST /trades`
    91	
    92	```json
    93	{ "symbol": "AAPL", "side": "Buy", "quantity": 100, "price": 187.25 }
    94	```
    95	
    96	- `201 Created`, `Location: /trades/{id}`, body = the created trade.
    97	- `400` ValidationProblemDetails for missing/invalid fields, unknown side, malformed JSON.
    98	- `415` for non-JSON content type (framework default).
    99	
   100	`GET /trades` → `200`, array of trades, newest first (`Timestamp` desc, then `Sequence` desc):
   101	
   102	```json
   103	[{ "id": "…", "symbol": "AAPL", "side": "Buy", "quantity": 100, "price": 187.25, "timestamp": "2026-10-19T14:03:11.123Z" }]
   104	```
   105	
   106	`GET /positions` → `200`, array sorted by symbol:
   107	
   108	```json
   109	[{ "symbol": "AAPL", "netQuantity": 100, "averageCost": 187.25 }]
   110	```
   111	
   112	Unhandled exceptions → `500` ProblemDetails, no stack trace outside Development. `GET /trades/{id}` is not required; `Location` still points there (my call: implement it as a trivial endpoint so the header is honest).
   113	
   114	Timestamps always serialize with a `Z` suffix. SQLite loses `DateTimeKind`, so the EF model needs a value converter that marks reads as UTC.
   115	
   116	Notional (`quantity * price`) is computed in the frontend, not sent by the API.
   117	
   118	Part 1 commits this contract as DTOs plus an OpenAPI document (Swashbuckle, exported to `docs/openapi.json`) and example payloads, so the frontend agent can build against a mock without waiting on the backend.
   119	
   120	### Backend architecture
   121	
   122	UI → Controller → Feature (business logic + data access).
   123	
   124	```
   125	backend/
   126	  TradeBlotter.sln
   127	  src/TradeBlotter.Api/
   128	    Controllers/        TradesController, PositionsController — HTTP only
   129	    Features/Trades/    trade service, request/response DTOs, validation
   130	    Features/Positions/ PositionCalculator (pure function), positions service
   131	    Data/               AppDbContext, entity config, migrations
   132	    Program.cs
   133	  tests/TradeBlotter.Api.Tests/   xUnit; unit + WebApplicationFactory integration tests
   134	```
   135	
   136	- EF Core 8 with SQLite, migrations committed. DB file `backend/src/TradeBlotter.Api/trade-blotter.db`, gitignored; connection string overridable via config/env (e2e uses a throwaway file).
   137	- SQLite stores `decimal` as TEXT and can't order or sum it in SQL. That's fine: positions are computed in memory. Order trades by `Timestamp` (ISO text sorts correctly).
   138	- `PositionCalculator` is a pure static function over a list of trades; it is the main mutation-testing target.
   139	
   140	### Frontend architecture
   141	
   142	```
   143	frontend/
   144	  src/
   145	    api/            fetch wrapper + trades/positions calls (no state)
   146	    stores/         Pinia: trades, positions
   147	    components/     Toolbar, BlotterGrid, SideCellRenderer, PositionsPanel, TradeEntryModal, TradeForm
   148	    App.vue, main.ts
   149	  e2e/              Playwright (Part 3)
   150	```
   151	
   152	- Vue 3 `<script setup>` + TypeScript, Vite, Pinia, PrimeVue (one theme preset, soft palette), AG Grid Community (`ag-grid-vue3`).
   153	- Layout uses CSS `display: grid` throughout: toolbar row on top, blotter in the main area, positions panel beside it.
   154	- Toolbar: search box (drives an AG Grid external filter via `isExternalFilterPresent` / `doesExternalFilterPass`) and a "+" button that opens the trade entry modal.
   155	- Blotter columns default to newest first, all sortable. Side uses a custom cell renderer: green Buy, red Sell. Timestamps are converted from UTC to the browser's local timezone with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.
   156	- Trade entry modal (PrimeVue Dialog) holds a single form: symbol, side, quantity, price. Small labels above inputs. Client-side validation mirrors the server's. Paste/bulk entry was considered and dropped (AG Grid's multi-cell paste is Enterprise-only).
   157	- Search box matches symbol and side, case-insensitive substring. (My call.)
   158	- After any successful POST  the trades and positions stores both re-fetch everything from the server. No optimistic insert, no `since` parameter.
   159	- Errors surface via PrimeVue Toast.
   160	- Dev server proxies `/trades` and `/positions` to the backend (no CORS config needed).
   161	- No timezone setting, no seed data.
   162	
   163	### Tooling and guardrails
   164	
   165	| Concern | Tool |
   166	|---|---|
   167	| C# format/lint | CSharpier |
   168	| JS/TS/Vue format/lint | Biome |
   169	| Unit tests | xUnit (backend), Vitest (frontend) |
   170	| Coverage ≥ 80% lines, enforced | coverlet threshold (backend), Vitest coverage thresholds (frontend) |
   171	| Mutation testing | Stryker.NET (backend `Features/**`), Stryker.js (frontend `src/stores`, `src/api`, pure helpers) |
   172	| Dead code / unused deps | knip |
   173	| Duplication | jscpd (both trees) |
   174	| File length | custom script: warn above 500 lines (soft; never blocks) |
   175	| Git hooks | lefthook |
   176	
   177	**Claude Code hooks** (`.claude/settings.json`): PostToolUse on Edit/Write/MultiEdit runs a script that formats and lints the touched file (Biome for `.ts/.js/.vue/.json`, CSharpier for `.cs`), then runs the file-length check. Lint errors exit 2 so the agent sees them.
   178	
   179	**Pre-commit** (lefthook): Biome and CSharpier on staged files, file-length check, then tests only for the side that changed (backend tests if `backend/**` is staged, frontend tests if `frontend/**`). knip and jscpd run on pre-push, not pre-commit, to keep commits fast.
   180	
   181	**Mutation testing is never on a hook.** Run on demand via scripts. Configure for speed:
   182	
   183	- Stryker.js: `stryker.config.mjs` with `testRunner: "vitest"`, `concurrency: os.availableParallelism() - 1`, `incremental: true` (incremental file gitignored), `ignoreStatic: true`, `mutate` restricted to logic files (exclude `.vue`, components, `main.ts`), no TypeScript checker. The vitest runner uses per-test coverage automatically.
   184	- Stryker.NET: `stryker-config.json` with `concurrency` set to cores − 1, `mutate` restricted to `Features/**`, `coverage-analysis: perTest`, `since` mode available for incremental runs. Installed as a local dotnet tool (`.config/dotnet-tools.json`).
   185	- Thresholds: high 80, low 60, break 50 for both.
   186	
   187	**MCP servers and skills** (`.mcp.json`, project-scoped): AG Grid, PrimeVue, Playwright. Verify package names at install time; drop any that don't exist rather than substituting a lookalike.
   188	
   189	### Repo files
   190	
   191	- `CLAUDE.md`: requirements summary, architecture rules (Controller → Feature, Pinia for state, `decimal` money, grid layout), commit rules (one meaningful change per commit, short imperative message), coverage rule, "update README whenever configuration changes", per-part section ownership.
   192	- `README.md`: setup (backend, frontend, tests, mutation, e2e), assumptions and design decisions, what's next. Skeleton in Part 1; each agent adds to its own section only.
   193	- `prompt.md`: the coordinator prompt, committed as-is.
   194	- `transcripts/`: every session's Claude Code `.jsonl` transcript, copied at the end, named by part. Scanned for secrets and absolute home paths before commit.
   195	- `.gitignore`: `bin/`, `obj/`, `node_modules/`, `*.db`, Stryker output and incremental files, Playwright reports.
   196	
   197	## Execution plan (coordination)
   198	
   199	Repo: `ensj/trade-blotter`, public. `main` is the integration branch.
   200	
   201	**Part 1 — skeleton (1 agent, on `main`).** Roughly one commit per bullet in `prompt.md`'s Part 1. A scaffold commit (empty .NET solution + test project, Vite app) goes right after CLAUDE.md so later configs have something to point at. Order: CLAUDE.md + README skeleton; project scaffold; skills/MCP; mutation testing config; hooks + linters; dev tools (knip, jscpd, file length); skeleton endpoints + DTOs + OpenAPI; data model + SQLite + EF migration. Skeleton endpoints return `501` or empty arrays. Coverage gates apply from the first commit with tests. Exit criteria: both projects build, hooks fire, pre-commit passes, OpenAPI committed.
   202	
   203	**Part 2 — parallel (2 agents, 2 worktrees).** Branches `feat/backend` and `feat/frontend` off Part 1's `main`. Each agent touches only its own tree plus its own README/CLAUDE.md section.
   204	
   205	- Backend: implement endpoints via features; position calculator with the worked-example tests; mutation testing on features; error handling and status codes.
   206	- Frontend: grid layout; AG Grid blotter with side renderer and external filter; Pinia stores + API module; toolbar and trade entry modal; positions panel; PrimeVue theme. Builds against a mock of the committed contract.
   207	
   208	**Part 3 — integrate and verify (coordinator + subagents, no extra herdr session).** Merge both branches into `main`. Playwright e2e against the real backend on a fresh DB, with screenshots of the full flow. A UI review pass on the screenshots (spacing, column order for a trader, label placement, grid sizing, consistent soft theme). A structure review (folders, Controller → Feature boundaries). Coverage subagents check every requirement in the exercise and `prompt.md` against the result. Copy transcripts, finish README, push.
   209	
   210	## Prerequisite
   211	
   212	.NET 8 SDK is not installed (only 6.0.401). Install it before Part 1.

   217	- Column widths and default column order (Part 3 reviews it).
   218	- Test file organization within each test project.
   219	- Exact jscpd threshold and knip config.

content.content:
1	# Trade Blotter
     2	
     3	A trade blotter: enter trades, see them in a live grid, and see positions derived from trade history. .NET 8 API + Vue 3 frontend.
     4	
     5	Design: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-trade-blotter-design.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-trade-blotter-design.md).
     6	
     7	## Setup
     8	
     9	### Prerequisites
    10	
    11	- .NET 8 SDK. `global.json` pins `8.0.x` with `rollForward: latestFeature`. If `dotnet` resolves to another SDK, put the right one first: `export DOTNET_ROOT=$HOME/.dotnet PATH=$HOME/.dotnet:$PATH`.
    12	- Node 24.
    13	
    14	### Claude Code MCP servers and skills
    15	
    16	- `.mcp.json` registers three project MCP servers, run through `npx`: AG Grid (`ag-mcp`), PrimeVue (`@primevue/mcp`) and Playwright (`@playwright/mcp`). Claude Code asks you to approve them on first use.
    17	- `.claude/skills/` holds the vendors' official skills, copied from [`ag-grid/skills`](https://github.com/ag-grid/skills) (`ag-dev`, `ag-update`) and [`primefaces/primeui-plugins`](https://github.com/primefaces/primeui-plugins/tree/main/plugins/primevue/skills) (`primevue-*`; these call the PrimeVue MCP tools). To update them, re-copy from those repos.
    18	
    19	### Backend
    20	
    21	```sh
    22	cd backend
    23	dotnet run --project src/TradeBlotter.Api   # http://localhost:5080, Swagger at /swagger
    24	```
    25	
    26	SQLite via EF Core 8. Migrations in `src/TradeBlotter.Api/Data/Migrations/` are applied on startup. The database file defaults to `src/TradeBlotter.Api/trade-blotter.db` (gitignored); override it with `ConnectionStrings__TradeBlotter="Data Source=/path/to/file.db"`.
    27	
    28	```sh
    29	dotnet tool restore
    30	dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/TradeBlotter.Api --output-dir Data/Migrations
    31	```
    32	
    33	Backend behavior worth knowing:
    34	
    35	- Validation lives in `Features/Trades/TradeValidator`, run by MVC through `CreateTradeRequest : IValidatableObject`, so every 400 has the same ValidationProblemDetails shape. Error keys are the camelCase JSON field names (`symbol`, `side`, `quantity`, `price`), set in `Http/ValidationProblemFactory` from MVC's JSON naming policy. `[Required]` reports missing fields; the validator checks values only once they are present.
    36	- Money must be a JSON number. `"quantity": "100"` is a 400, not coerced.
    37	- SQLite stores decimals as TEXT and reads `100` back as `100.0`, so responses may carry a trailing `.0`. The value is identical.
    38	- 500s are ProblemDetails with no exception detail outside Development.
    39	
    40	Mutation score (Stryker.NET 4.16.0, `Features/**`, 2026-10-20): **97.92%**, 47 killed, 1 survived, 0 timeouts. 13 mutants did not compile and 4 were skipped as already covered; neither counts.
    41	
    42	| File | Killed | Survived |
    43	|---|---|---|
    44	| `Positions/PositionCalculator.cs` | 22 | 1 |
    45	| `Positions/PositionService.cs` | 1 | 0 |
    46	| `Trades/TradeService.cs` | 5 | 0 |
    47	| `Trades/TradeValidator.cs` | 19 | 0 |
    48	
    49	Remaining survivor:
    50	
    51	- `PositionCalculator`: `q <= held` → `q < held`. Equivalent. When a trade closes the position to exactly zero, the mutant keeps the trade price as the average instead of the old one, but a zero position is omitted and the next trade starts fresh because `held` is 0, so no output changes.
    52	
    53	### Frontend
    54	
    55	```sh
    56	cd frontend
    57	npm install
    58	npm run dev     # http://localhost:5173; proxies /trades and /positions to the backend on 5080
    59	npm run dev:mock  # same, but serves /trades and /positions from an in-memory mock (frontend/mock/), no backend
    60	npm run build
    61	```
    62	
    63	- **Layout.** `src/App.vue` is a CSS grid: toolbar row, blotter, positions panel beside it (stacked below 900px). The PrimeVue Aura preset uses a sky primary, and the AG Grid Quartz theme reads the same PrimeVue CSS variables (`src/theme.ts`). Dark mode is off.
    64	- **Code map.** `src/api/` holds stateless fetch calls (ProblemDetails → `ApiError`). `src/stores/` holds the Pinia `trades` and `positions` stores; a successful create re-fetches both. `src/lib/` has pure helpers: formatting, search matching, and validation that mirrors the server. `src/components/` holds the views.
    65	- **Search** matches symbol or side as a case-insensitive substring, through an AG Grid external filter.
    66	- **Mutation score** (Stryker.js on `src/stores` and `src/api`, 2026-10-20): 91.80% (56 killed, 5 survived, 0 no coverage). Survivors: three stale-response guards in `src/stores/resource.ts` (`--latest` is equivalent; the error and loading guards are not asserted for an overlapping failure) and, in `src/api/http.ts`, the `ApiError` name and the `status` in the fallback problem body.
    67	
    68	### API contract
    69	
    70	- `docs/openapi.json`: the OpenAPI document exported from Swashbuckle. A backend test fails if it drifts from the running app; regenerate it with `UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 dotnet test backend`.
    71	- `docs/examples/`: request, response and validation-error payloads. A backend test deserializes them into the DTOs.
    72	- `frontend/src/api/types.ts`: TypeScript mirror of the contract.
    73	
    74	### Tests
    75	
    76	```sh
    77	cd backend && dotnet test   # xUnit; fails below 80% line coverage (coverlet; Program.cs and Migrations excluded)
    78	cd frontend && npm test     # Vitest; fails below 80% lines/branches/functions/statements
    79	```
    80	
    81	### Lint, format and hooks
    82	
    83	```sh
    84	cd frontend && npx biome check .                        # Biome: format + lint TS/JS/Vue/JSON
    85	dotnet tool restore && dotnet csharpier check backend   # CSharpier (local tool in .config/dotnet-tools.json)
    86	lefthook install                                        # once per clone (also run by `npm install` in frontend)
    87	```
    88	
    89	- **pre-commit** (lefthook): Biome and CSharpier fix staged files, the file-length check warns, then `dotnet test` runs if `backend/**` is staged and `npm test` if `frontend/**` is staged.
    90	- **Claude Code** (`.claude/settings.json`): after every Edit/Write/MultiEdit, `scripts/claude-post-edit.sh` formats and lints the file and runs the file-length check. Lint errors exit 2 so the agent sees them.
    91	- **pre-push** (lefthook): knip (unused files, exports and dependencies in `frontend/`, config `frontend/knip.jsonc`) and jscpd (duplication across `backend/` and `frontend/src`, fails above 3%, config `.jscpd.json`).
    92	- `scripts/check-file-length.sh [files]` warns about files over 500 lines and never fails; with no arguments it checks every tracked file.
    93	- Run the dev tools directly with `npm run lint`, `npm run knip` and `npm run dup` in `frontend/`.
    94	- `scripts/dotnet-env.sh` puts `~/.dotnet` first on PATH, since git hooks don't read shell profiles. `scripts/with-dotnet.sh` (hooks) and `scripts/mutation-backend.sh` source it.
    95	
    96	### Mutation testing
    97	
    98	On demand only, never on a hook. Thresholds: high 80, low 60, break 50.
    99

     2	
     3	A trade blotter: enter trades, see them in a live grid, and see positions derived from trade history. .NET 8 API + Vue 3 frontend.

Error keys are the camelCase JSON field names (`symbol`, `side`, `quantity`, `price`), set in `Http/ValidationProblemFactory` from MVC's JSON naming policy. `[Required]` reports missing fields; the validator checks values only once they are present.
    36	- Money must be a JSON number. `"quantity": "100"` is a 400, not coerced.
    37	- SQLite stores decimals as TEXT and reads `100` back as `100.0`, so responses may carry a trailing `.0`. The value is identical.
    38	- 500s are ProblemDetails with no exception detail outside Development.

    44	| `Positions/PositionCalculator.cs` | 22 | 1 |

1	import type { CreateTradeRequest, ProblemDetails, Side } from '../api/types'
     2	
     3	// Mirrors the server's rules; the server stays the authority.
     4	export type TradeField = 'symbol' | 'side' | 'quantity' | 'price'
     5	export type FieldErrors = Partial<Record<TradeField, string>>
     6	
     7	export interface TradeDraft {
     8	  symbol: string
     9	  side: Side | null
    10	  quantity: number | null
    11	  price: number | null
    12	}
    13	
    14	const SYMBOL = /^[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,10}$/
    15	const MAX_AMOUNT = 1_000_000_000
    16	const FIELDS: TradeField[] = ['symbol', 'side', 'quantity', 'price']
    17	
    18	function amountError(value: number | null, label: string): string | undefined {
    19	  if (value === null || !Number.isFinite(value)) return `${label} is required`
    20	  if (value <= 0) return 'Must be greater than 0'
    21	  if (value > MAX_AMOUNT) return 'Must be at most 1,000,000,000'
    22	  if (Number(value.toFixed(4)) !== value) return 'At most 4 decimal places'
    23	  return undefined
    24	}
    25	
    26	export function validateTrade(draft: TradeDraft): FieldErrors {
    27	  const errors: FieldErrors = {}
    28	  const symbol = draft.symbol.trim()
    29	  if (!symbol) errors.symbol = 'Symbol is required'
    30	  else if (!SYMBOL.test(symbol)) errors.symbol = "Use 1–10 letters, digits, '.' or '-'"
    31	  if (!draft.side) errors.side = 'Side is required'
    32	  const quantity = amountError(draft.quantity, 'Quantity')
    33	  if (quantity) errors.quantity = quantity
    34	  const price = amountError(draft.price, 'Price')
    35	  if (price) errors.price = price
    36	  return errors
    37	}
    38	
    39	export function toRequest(draft: TradeDraft): CreateTradeRequest {
    40	  if (!draft.side || draft.quantity === null || draft.price === null) {
    41	    throw new Error('toRequest needs a validated draft')
    42	  }
    43	  return {
    44	    symbol: draft.symbol.trim().toUpperCase(),
    45	    side: draft.side,
    46	    quantity: draft.quantity,
    47	    price: draft.price,
    48	  }
    49	}

I found five gaps. Nothing in the code contradicts the design: there is no users table, no client timestamp or timezone, no paste mode, and money is decimal throughout.

**Missing**
1. **No `transcripts/` directory.** The design requires it (spec:194, 208). Fix: copy each session's `.jsonl` into `transcripts/` named by part, scrub secrets and home paths, then commit.
2. **README's last two sections are empty.** "Assumptions and design decisions" and "What's next" are bare headings (README.md:124-126), and both the exercise and the spec (spec:13, 192) require them. Fix: fill them from the spec's Decisions and Non-goals, e.g. decimal money, the average-cost rule, rounding to 6 places, no users, no paste, no pagination, refresh after submit instead of push.

**Partial**
3. **Stryker.NET concurrency is not in the config.** The spec puts it in `stryker-config.json` (spec:184), but `backend/stryker-config.json:1-10` has none; only `scripts/mutation-backend.sh:8` sets cores − 1. CLAUDE.md:26 tells agents to run `dotnet stryker` directly, which skips that setting. Fix: point CLAUDE.md:26 at `scripts/mutation-backend.sh`, or put a fixed `"concurrency"` in the config.
4. **README misstates the Stryker.js scope.** README.md:66 says the score covers `src/stores` and `src/api`. The config (`frontend/stryker.config.mjs:6-13`) mutates all of `src/**/*.ts` except components, so `src/lib` and `theme.ts` are included (README.md:103 says this correctly). Fix: re-run `npm run mutation` and update the score line with the real scope.
5. **The Claude edit hook skips files outside `frontend/` and `backend/`.** `scripts/claude-post-edit.sh:10,16` only matches those two trees, so root JSON like `.mcp.json` and `.jscpd.json` is never linted. It also needs `jq`, and if `jq` is missing the hook exits 0 without doing anything (line 6-7). Fix: add a case that runs Biome on root `*.json`, and fail loudly when `jq` is absent, or list it in the README prerequisites.

**Commit hygiene:** acceptable. Subjects are short and imperative, and most commits hold one change. Two blemishes:
- `a454a35` bundles Biome, CSharpier, the edit hook and lefthook. This matches the prompt's "one bullet per commit".
- `4048f56` (adding a PrimeUI license key) was undone by `02f565e`. That is churn, not a rule break.

Nothing to fix.

**Fully covered:**
- **Repo setup:** CLAUDE.md (rules, commits, README-update rule, 80% coverage, ownership); `.mcp.json` with AG Grid, PrimeVue and Playwright, plus vendor skills.
- **Guardrails:** Stryker.js (concurrency, incremental, scoped mutate, thresholds); PostToolUse hook in `.claude/settings.json`; lefthook pre-commit (Biome, CSharpier, file length, tests per side) and pre-push (knip, jscpd); 500-line soft check; coverlet and Vitest 80% gates.
- **Backend:** all endpoints, including `GET /trades/{id}` with 201 + Location, ProblemDetails and 415; Trade model with Sequence, UTC converter and decimal; SQLite, EF and the committed migration; Controller → Features split; the worked-example tests.
- **Frontend:** custom Side renderer; external-filter search; Pinia stores that re-fetch both after a POST; toolbar and PrimeVue Dialog form with labels above inputs; positions panel; `display: grid` throughout; PrimeVue theme shared with AG Grid; Toast errors; Vite proxy.
- **E2e:** runs against the real stack on a fresh DB, with seven screenshots in `docs/screenshots/`.
